claims.text: Ambiguity is not a whim of philosophy nor a fault but belongs to the positive essence of metaphysics; the preliminary appraisal is incomplete until this ambiguity is indicated.

Philosophy presents itself as and looks like a science yet is not, and presents itself as the proclamation of a worldview yet is not; this dual semblance brings about a constant insecurity in philosophy.
The ambiguity becomes more acute, rather than vanishing, precisely where we are explicitly concerned with it — as in our here-and-now situation of philosophy taught as an examination subject.
The teacher is not exempt from ambiguity; by presenting himself as a teacher he brings a semblance with him, and a dubious authority silently persuades only so long as he is not understood.

The attempt to overcome ambiguity by limiting things to what is provable rests on the presupposition that what is essential is whatever can be proven — yet perhaps what is provable is only what is essentially irrelevant.

Mathematical knowledge is the emptiest and least binding knowledge as regards human substance, and so cannot become the measure for the richest and most binding knowledge imaginable: philosophical knowledge.

The formal-contradiction argument ('to assert with absolute certainty that there is no absolute certainty refutes itself') is completely empty and non-binding; we never claim it is absolutely certain that philosophy is not a science.

Philosophy has meaning only as a human activity; its truth is essentially that of human Dasein, and is in part rooted in the fate of Dasein, which occurs in freedom amid possibilities, change, and predicament it does not control.
Philosophy is the opposite of all comfort and assurance: it is turbulence (Wirbel) into which man is spun, and constantly remains in the perilous neighbourhood of supreme uncertainty.

We must hold out in the terror (Schrecken), for in it becomes manifest that in the philosophical concept man as a whole is in the grip of an attack (Angriff); the attacker is not everyday man but the Da-sein in man.
The normal human being takes his petty pleasures, shallow fears, and smug comforts as the measure of joy, terror, and security; philosophizing may not be dragged before such a judge.

Philosophy does not exist because there are sciences; rather there can be sciences only because there is philosophy — philosophizing is itself a fundamental way of Da-sein that lets Da-sein first become what it can be.

Philosophizing lies prior to every occupation and constitutes the fundamental occurrence of Dasein, something autonomous that stands on its own and is quite different from our common kinds of comportment.

one_sentence: Chapter Two of the Preliminary Appraisal (§§4-7) interprets the threefold ambiguity (Zweideutigkeit) of philosophizing — science-or-worldview in general, listener-and-teacher here-and-now, and the truth of philosophy as such — and resolves it not by abolishing the ambiguity but by relocating philosophy's truth in the fate (Geschick) of Dasein, so that philosophizing emerges as turbulence and terror, an autonomous fundamental occurrence (Grundgeschehen) of Da-sein that grounds the later demand to awaken an attunement.

boredom_bridge.summary: fcm-01 is the methodological-foundational unit: it does not yet analyze boredom but secures the conditions under which the boredom-spine (Chs. 2-5) can proceed. Its load-bearing contribution to the King-Salvo bridge is the principle that philosophy's truth 'cannot be decided on the purely factual grounds of proof,' that it is 'turbulence' rooted in the fate of Dasein and never a present-at-hand matter of fact — the same epistemic register that, transposed onto the empirical work, warns that a fundamental attunement (boredom) cannot be read off a single instrument value but must be approached through questioning. The chapter also installs the affective vocabulary the boredom analysis will inherit: terror (Schrecken), being in the grip of an attack (Angriff), turbulence (Wirbel), and the contrast between the 'normal' human's smug comforts and the perilous neighbourhood of supreme uncertainty.
